title: Share GMCP bootstrap registration without losing tool behavior
goal: Vision: V-6. susi core must be less than 100k lines. no functionalities must be dropped. susi core is a pure standards protocol compliant ai os socket. Consolidate repetitive registration code while preserving all 204 tools, exact metadata, categories, handlers, ordering and feature gates.

reuse.searched: crates/susi-daemon/src/gmcp_bootstrap.rs: 204 repeated register_meta_tool calls; crates/susi-tools/src/registry.rs: shared ToolRegistry::register_meta_tool already dual-registers capabilities; crates/susi-gmcp/src/tools/args.rs and tool_def!: descriptions differ from registry contract; Cargo.lock: no dependency changes needed
reuse.reason: Reuse existing public registration and CoreTools handlers through one typed descriptor loop; preserve exact registry descriptions rather than merge different catalogs.

coordination: Parent owns integration and Board coordination. Isolated worktree; no commits, pushes or external messages by this worker.

results.metadata: All names, exact registry descriptions, categories, handler pointers, order and feature gates match fixture captured from pristine base before editing. Both registries retain exact metadata.
results.shared_implementation: 204 generic registration closures replaced by one typed function-pointer registration loop.

limitations: ambient_pulse remains tools-rich-only in MCP, as before; CLI exposes it in every build. Socket parity now explicitly verifies this existing feature-dependent availability instead of falsely counting disabled source declarations. KNOWN_GAPS unchanged.
Function pointer comparison supplements exact macro-derived name/handler binding and executable success/error probes; function addresses alone are not a semantic identity guarantee.
Focused validation is not full release qualification and does not establish the whole-core 100k goal.
peer_review: Independent read-only review confirmed pristine 204 descriptor parity, unchanged 5 existing tests, narrow rich reference fixes and physical LOC counts.
